method: Public evidence only. Official acknowledgement, reproduction, a shipped change, and post-fix verification are recorded separately.

issues.title: Persistent Recon markers
issues.bottom_line: Patch 1.3 improved it, but developers have not called it resolved. Server restarts may clear it temporarily.
issues.symptom: Enemy markers created by Recon Planes and Flares can remain on the Tactical Map longer than intended.
issues.official_position: The developers acknowledged increased reports and shipped improvements in Patch 1.3, but explicitly declined to call the issue resolved because the reported behavior remained difficult to reproduce internally.
issues.workaround: For community-server owners, rebooting the server will typically clear persistent markers when the issue occurs.
known: Changes intended to improve the behavior shipped in Patch 1.3.
A server reboot is an official temporary workaround for community servers.
The developers are monitoring a possible server-side degradation factor.
unknown: The root cause has not been publicly established.
It is not known whether every persistent-marker report has the same cause.
There is no public declaration that Patch 1.3 fully resolved the issue.

timeline.detail: Developers report increased player reports, difficult internal reproduction, and improvements prepared for Patch 1.3.
The planned improvements ship; the issue remains under observation rather than closed.
The team mentions a possible server-side degradation factor and says it will monitor post-patch behavior.

sources.claim: Acknowledged; improvements prepared; further investigation ongoing

sources.claim: Patch containing the planned improvements shipped

issues.title: Robotic Proximity VOIP
issues.bottom_line: A candidate fix tested positively and was targeted for Patch 1.4, subject to further testing.
issues.symptom: Proximity Chat can sound distorted or robotic, reducing the usefulness of local voice communication.
issues.official_position: The team said it was working with its external VOIP partner at Epic Games, believed a fix had been identified, and had seen positive initial test results. Larger-scale testing was still required.
known: The investigation involves the external VOIP partner at Epic Games.
A candidate fix produced positive initial results.
Patch 1.4 was a target, subject to testing—not a guaranteed release commitment.
unknown: The exact failing component has not been publicly identified.
The public material reviewed does not establish that the candidate fix has shipped.
It is not established that every VOIP failure report is this specific robotic-audio defect.

timeline.detail: VOIP and wider audio problems are elevated among major community-reported issues.
A candidate fix is identified with positive initial results; larger-scale testing begins.
The candidate fix is not included; Patch 1.4 remains the stated target subject to testing.

issues.title: AMD-associated crashes
issues.bottom_line: This is several crash problems, not one AMD bug. Disabling gore may reduce their frequency.
issues.symptom: Some client crashes appear more frequently on systems using AMD graphics hardware.
issues.official_position: The developers describe multiple individual stability problems—not one universal AMD bug—and say they are working directly with AMD. Improvements are expected to arrive incrementally as individual causes are identified.
issues.workaround: Disabling gore is the only mitigation publicly identified by the developers in the reviewed update; they say it will likely reduce crash frequency for affected players.
known: The developers acknowledge a higher frequency of some crashes on AMD hardware.
Several individual stability problems have been identified.
The development team says it is working directly with AMD.
Disabling gore is an official mitigation, not a guaranteed fix.
unknown: A crash occurring on AMD hardware cannot automatically be assigned to this issue family.
No single public root cause explains all reports.
The proportion of AMD users affected is not publicly established.

timeline.detail: Stability, including AMD-associated crashes, is identified as a major feedback area.
Developers report progress on multiple individual issues, direct work with AMD, and the gore-disabled mitigation.
Further stability and performance work ships; the broader AMD-associated family remains open.

sources.title: Community Update #2
sources.claim: Multiple causes, direct AMD collaboration, and gore-disabled mitigation documented

sources.title: Patch 1.3
sources.claim: Additional client and server stability work shipped

issues.title: Invisible prop collision
issues.bottom_line: Team17 received a specific report and Patch 1.3 fixed some extended collision, but exact assets are unconfirmed.
issues.symptom: Bullets can be blocked by invisible collision between visible gaps in fences, chairs, tables, and other props.
issues.official_position: Team17 Support requested map and location details for a direct report. Separately, Patch 1.3 shipped more than 100 map fixes across six maps, including extended collision. The public evidence does not link every reported prop to a particular patch item.
known: A specific fence-and-furniture report was received by Team17 Support.
Support requested exact map and location information for investigation.
Patch 1.3 documents a broad set of map fixes that includes extended collision.
unknown: A support response is not proof that developers reproduced the exact report.
It is not known which individual assets were included in the Patch 1.3 collision fixes.
Different props or maps may represent separate defects.

timeline.detail: A Steam Report a Problem thread documents bullets blocked by gaps in fences and furniture.
Support asks for exact maps and locations so the team can investigate.
More than 100 map fixes ship, with extended collision named as one addressed issue class.

issues.title: VIP list removed on reset
issues.bottom_line: Patch 1.3 says VIP lists now survive server resets. Independent verification is not yet recorded here.
issues.symptom: Resetting a community server could remove its VIP list.
issues.official_position: Patch 1.3 explicitly states that VIP lists are now retained following server resets. The defect class and shipped change are clear; independent post-patch verification is not included in the reviewed official record.
known: The defect class is confirmed by official patch notes.
A fix shipped in Patch 1.3 on August 28.
The same patch also corrected VIP comments not appearing as intended.
unknown: The underlying technical cause was not published.
The patch note alone does not prove that every historical SoulSniper VIP incident was this defect.
Independent post-patch verification has not yet been recorded in this tracker.

timeline.detail: VIP lists are changed to remain intact following community-server resets; VIP comments are also corrected.
